thread.title: Apple Reverses Lower As Stocks Sell Off, But Bitcoin Holds Gains

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Apple Reverses Lower As Stocks Sell Off, But Bitcoin Holds Gains
text:
Stocks plunged Thursday amid continued volatility as Intel ( INTC ) and American Express ( AXP ) weighed on the Dow Jones industrials. Apple ( AAPL ) reversed lower.
X PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) tumbled 2.2%, SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) sank 2.2%% and SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) dropped 1.9%. ProShares UltraPro Short QQQ ( SQQQ ), an inverse leveraged fund, soared 6.7%.
Semiconductors, biotechs and homebuilders led the downside among sector plays in the stock market today . Gold miners bucked the decline.
Intel and AmEx were among the Dow's biggest losers, down nearly 4% each. Apple had been one of the earlier holdouts with a small gain, but reversed lower as it continues testing the 200-day line. The iPhone maker slid Wednesday amid a neutral rating from Goldman Sachs.
Oil ETFs were lower along with West Texas intermediate crude prices. Gold funds advanced as gold futures rose 0.5% to $1,318.30 an ounce.
Bitcoin extended a recent rebound, gaining 10% to $8,376.22, according to CoinDesk . The cryptocurrency earlier climbed to $8,621.28. Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ) halved its gain to 3% but remains on track for a third straight advance after finding support at its 200-day line on Tuesday. Japan will conduct more inspections of domestic cryptocurrency exchanges, following the massive Jan. 26 Coincheck hack.
Banking On Banks? Bank stocks, which got a nice post-presidential election boost, rose to record highs last month.
They've since pulled back along with the broader market. But a pair of bank ETFs may be in potential buy range as they find support at their 50-day moving average lines.
SPDR S&P Bank ( KBE ) breached its 50-day during Monday's rout, recovered it the next session and added to gains on Wednesday. That puts it in a potential buy zone from a rebound off the support line. Shares advanced 15% from a late-November bounce off the 50-day to their Jan. 24 intraday high.
Banks are expected to be beneficiaries of higher interest rates. But don't forget: All purchases are riskier than usual now with the market uptrend under pressure.
The $4.1 billion fund, which marked its 12th anniversary in November, tracks the S&P Banks Select Industry Index. The index comprises asset management and custody banks, diversified banks, regional banks and other related subindustries. Regional banks accounted for nearly 77% of assets as of Feb. 6, while diversified banks and thrifts & mortgage finance made up about 9% each. Asset management and custody banks represented 4%; other diversified financial services rounded out the portfolio.
Top holdings included Puerto Rico's Popular ( BPOP ), Regions Financial ( RF ), Signature Bank ( SBNY ) and Comerica ( CMA ). KBE's 3.4% year-to-date return through Feb. 7, according to Morningstar Direct, is   flat performance. Its average annual returns of 16.1% and 15.3%, respectively,   years are slightly ahead of the benchmark index's gains for those periods.
